newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Top Danish banks' 1996 profits seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Top Danish banks' 1996 profits seen lower.

text.p: Eight international and domestic analysts polled by Reuters forecast falling average profits for Denmark's big four banks in 1996 in a survey issued on Monday.

The panel estimated that foreign exchange and securities earnings of the top three banks, Den Danske Bank, Unidanmark and BG Bank, fell by an average 20 percent last year, with profit before tax and extraordinary items 10 percent down on 1995.

Den Danske Bank is Denmark's biggest bank, followed in second place by Unidanmark, with BG Bank, which was formed from a merger of the former post office Giro Bank and Bikuben savings bank on January 1, 1996, the third largest.

Although the fourth biggest bank Jyske Bank was also seen posting lower foreign exchange and securities earnings for last year as well, it was seen as emerging with an improved pre-tax and extraordinary items profit.

Jyske Bank's result is the easiest for analysts to foresee as it is the only one of Denmark's leading banks to issue quarterly results. The four major banks are to release their full year 1996 results in mid-to-late February.

The panel forecast an average Jyske Bank 1996 pre-tax and extraordinary profit just short of one billion crowns, with the surplus at Den Danske Bank at 4.8 billion crowns, the largest profit of all the banks.

The panel foresaw lower operating costs last year for Den Danske Bank and BG Bank, with Unidanmark and Jyske Bank expected to report higher costs, pointing to dividends as an interesting item in the upcoming top four bank results.

"Foreign investors watch dividends closely when they invest in Danish bank paper. The more foreign investors our banks have, the more this puts pressure on them to raise dividends," said one analyst, who declined to be named.

The panel foresaw higher 1996 dividends with Den Danske Bank giving shareholders the best return of all and BG Bank, which attracted a considerable number of foreign investors in a major share issue last year, set to increase its dividend by 100 percent on average to 10 crowns per share.
Unidanmark is due to announce its full year 1996 result on February 19, followed by Jyske Bank and Den Danske Bank on February 20, and BG Bank on February 24.
